text.p: The Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) board meets on Tuesday, April 1.
Ahead of the meeting, Reuters asked 30 economists the following questions
1) Are you expecting a change in official interest rates to follow the April board meeting?
2) What direction do you expected the next move in interest rates will most likely be?
3) When will the next rate move take place?

The most likely scenario for Australian interest rates, based on current information, is that they will remain in hold for at least most of 1997, before rising in the face of emerging inflation pressures, economists said.
These result are very similar to those from the survey ahead of the March board meeting.

With partial indicators suggesting stronger growth can be expected later in 1997, and most economists feeling underlying inflation will trough in the middle of the year, the chances of a rate cut are declining.
National Mutual still see room for a rate cut in May, which would follow first quarter inflation and wages data, as they have a fairly low inflation outlook.

Others said that while inflation would remain low, the increasing pace of activity was likely to create some price pressures, and belived the RBA would be vigiliant in protecting its low inflation record of the 1990s.
The U.S. Federal Reserve's move to lift interest rates to 5.50 percent has had no impact on forecasts for local rates, economists said.
